facts.statement: The fossil material of Doolysaurus was discovered in 2023 by Hyemin Jo on Aphae Island in South Korea.
facts.quote: The Doolysaurus fossil material was discovered in 2023 by Hyemin Jo in outcrops of the Ilseongsan Formation on Aphae Island of Shinan, South Korea.

facts.statement: The genus name Doolysaurus honors a Korean cartoon character and the Ancient Greek word for lizard.
facts.quote: The generic name, Doolysaurus, combines a reference to "Dooly the Little Dinosaur", a Korean cartoon dinosaur character, with the Ancient Greek σαῦρος (sauros), meaning lizard.

facts.statement: The species name huhmini honors paleontologist Min Huh for his work on Korean dinosaurs.
facts.quote: The specific name, huhmini, honors paleontologist Min Huh, and his contributions to dinosaur research in Korea.

facts.statement: The holotype specimen includes an incomplete but three-dimensionally preserved skeleton with skull, spine, forelimb, and hindlimb remains.
facts.quote: The specimen consists of an incomplete, yet three-dimensionally preserved, skeleton, including remains of the skull, vertebral column, forelimb, and hindlimb.

facts.statement: Doolysaurus lived during the Albian to Cenomanian stages of the Cretaceous period.
Doolysaurus is known from the Ilseongsan Formation of South Korea, dating to the Albian to lower Cenomanian.
facts.quote: Doolysaurus is an extinct genus of thescelosaurid ornithischian dinosaur known from the Cretaceous (Albian–lower Cenomanian) Ilseongsan Formation of South Korea.

facts.statement: Doolysaurus is classified as a thescelosaurid ornithischian dinosaur.
Phylogenetic analyses place Doolysaurus within the family Thescelosauridae.
facts.quote: In their phylogenetic analyses, Jung et al. (2026) recovered Doolysaurus as a member of the family Thescelosauridae using the dataset of Fonseca et al. (2024).

facts.statement: Doolysaurus belongs to the subfamily Thescelosaurinae.
Results of phylogenetic analyses vary depending on the dataset used, with some placing Doolysaurus in Orodrominae and others in Thescelosaurinae.
facts.quote: When the sensitivity of the analysis based on the dataset of Fonseca et al. (2024) was tested with the dataset of Avrahami et al. (2024), Doolysaurus was also placed within Thescelosauridae in both the 50% majority-rule consensus parsimony analysis and the Bayesian analysis, the former of which recovered this taxon within Orodrominae and Koreanosaurus within Thescelosaurinae instead.
